sources.entry: Background Music - Control app volumes and record system audio. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kyleneideck/BackgroundMusic)
Background Music - Background Music, a macOS audio utility: automatically pause your music, set individual apps' volumes and record system audio.

summary.one_liner: Background Music is a macOS audio utility that auto-pauses your music player when other audio plays, sets per-app volumes, and records system audio.
summary.what_it_does: It automatically pauses a supported music player when a second audio source starts and unpauses it when that source stops. It provides a volume slider for each running application, with the ability to boost quiet apps above their normal maximum. It installs a virtual audio device so system audio can be recorded, for example via QuickTime Player, or combined with a microphone using an aggregate device in Audio MIDI Setup. It sets itself as the default output device at startup and restores the previous one on quit. The README says it is still in alpha.
use_cases: automatically pause music when a video or call starts
control individual app volume on a Mac
boost volume of a quiet application
record system audio together with a microphone
mix music and notification sounds on a Mac
how_to_run: Download BackgroundMusic-0.5.0.pkg from the README's download section and install it
Or clone the repository and run: /bin/bash build_and_install.sh (requires Xcode 10 or higher)
To uninstall: cd /Applications/Background\ Music.app/Contents/Resources/ and run bash uninstall.sh
notable: Auto-pauses and unpauses supported music players such as iTunes, Spotify, VLC, and Swinsian
Per-application volume sliders with boost above maximum
Installs a virtual audio device usable as a recording input in QuickTime Player
Available via Homebrew cask or a .pkg installer
Based on Apple's Core Audio User-Space Driver sample code
caveats: Still in alpha according to the README
Requires macOS 10.13 or later; only 2-channel stereo output devices are supported
Setting an app's volume above 50% can cause clipping; some issues with VLC, Skype, and Chrome are listed as known issues
